literal: Sharing food, having accustomed himself to it, him, hunger called fiery-disease, touching, is rare.
translation: The fiery disease of hunger will never touch the one who has made a habit of sharing his food with others.
modern: தன் உணவைப் பிறரோடு பகிர்ந்து உண்ணும் பழக்கத்தைக் கொண்டவனை, பசி என்று சொல்லப்படும் கொடிய நோய் தீண்டுவது இல்லை.
explanation: This couplet highlights the protective power of charity. The poet compares hunger to a 'fiery disease' (தீப்பிணி) because of the intense, burning pain and suffering it inflicts on the body. The word 'மரீஇ' indicates a deep-seated habit or custom; it is not about a one-time act of giving, but rather about someone who has integrated sharing into their daily life. The couplet assures us that such a generous person will never suffer from the misery of hunger, as their virtue and the goodwill of those they helped will always sustain them.
